annotation.speech2: The same triangular region with two horizontal arrows. A vermillion arrow at height y equals zero point three crosses the region and its right end lies on the green line x equals two y. A reddish purple arrow at height y equals zero point seven five crosses the region and its right end lies on the blue line x equals two minus two y. A dashed line at y equals one half separates the two cases.
A horizontal strip below y equals one half. Its right end lies on the line x equals 2 y.
A horizontal strip above y equals one half. Its right end lies on the line x equals 2 minus 2 y.
The dashed line y equals one half where the right boundary changes from one line to the other, forcing a split into two integrals.
